 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Association**, also known as the **Indian Association**, was the first avowed nationalist organization founded in **British India**.
 
• It was established on **July 26, 1876**, in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**), **West Bengal**, by **Surendranath Banerjee** and **Ananda Mohan Bose**. ***Hence, statement C is correct.***
 
• The association was founded to promote the political, intellectual, and material advancement of the people of **India** by every legitimate means.
 
• It aimed to create a strong body of public opinion in the country and unify the **Indian** people on a common political program and interests.
 
• The association attracted the **educated middle class** and became a platform for the protest against the **pro-British** policies of the **landed aristocracy** represented by the **British Indian Association**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale**: **Dadabhai Naoroji**, known as the "Grand Old Man of India," founded the **East India Association** in **London** in **1866** to lobby for **Indian** interests. **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** was a moderate leader who founded the **Servants of India Society** in **1905** in **Pune**. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji and Debendranath Tagore**: **Debendranath Tagore** was a prominent leader of the **Brahmo Samaj** and was instrumental in the formation of the **British Indian Association** in **1851**, which primarily represented the interests of **Zamindars**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal**: These leaders were the pillars of the **Extremist** faction within the **Indian National Congress**. **Tilak** started the **Home Rule League** in **1916**, and **Bipin Chandra Pal** was a major figure in the **Swadeshi Movement** of **1905**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***
 
• The **Indian National Association** played a crucial role in agitating against the **Vernacular Press Act** of **1878** and the **Arms Act**.
 
• Due to overlapping goals, the **Indian National Association** merged with the **Indian National Congress** (founded in **1885**) during its second session held in **Calcutta** in **1886**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Civil Service Agitation**: One of the earliest successes of the **Indian National Association** was the agitation against the lowering of the **age limit** for the **Indian Civil Service** (ICS) examination from **21** to **19** **years** in **1877**.
 
• **First All-India Conference**: The association organized the first **All-India National Conference** in **1883**, which served as a precursor to the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee** was a former **ICS** officer who was dismissed by the **British**, which fueled his resolve to build a national political organization.
 
• **Ananda Mohan Bose** was the first **Indian Wrangler** (a student who gains first-class honors in the Mathematical Tripos) of **Cambridge University** and later served as the **President** of the **Indian National Congress** in **1898**.

questions.question: The ages (in years) of patients in a clinic are recorded as follows: 15 , 18 , 21 , 21 , 23 , 25 , 28 , 30 , 35 , 40 , 45 , 50 , 55. Calculate the difference between the median age now and after removing the oldest patient (55 years) from the data set.

questions.question: Under which Act were the Environment Audit Rules, 2025, issued on 29-8-2025?

options.text: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** serves as the **umbrella legislation** in **India**, providing a framework for the **Central Government** to coordinate the activities of various central and state authorities established under other laws like the **Water Act** and **Air Act**.
 
• Under **Section 6** and **Section 25** of this Act, the **Government of India** has the power to make rules for the protection of the environment, which includes the notification of **Environment Audit Rules** or **Environmental Statement** requirements to monitor industrial impact. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• The **Environment (Protection) Act** was enacted in the wake of the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** of **1984**, which highlighted the urgent need for comprehensive environmental safety regulations and **industrial auditing** mechanisms.
 
• The Act was passed in **March 1986** and came into force on **19 November 1986**, coinciding with the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**, who was a key proponent of environmental conservation.
 
• The **Environment Audit Rules** (often referred to as the submission of an **Environmental Statement**) require industries to provide an annual account of **resource consumption**, **pollution generated**, and **waste management** practices to the **State Pollution Control Boards**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**:

 
 
• This Act provides for the protection of **wild animals, birds, and plants** to ensure the **ecological and environmental security** of **India**.
 
• It established schedules of **protected species** and prohibits hunting while regulating trade in wildlife products. It is not the parent act for industrial environment audits.
 
 
 
• **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980**:
 
 
• Enacted to check the **deforestation** of **forest land** for **non-forestry purposes**, this Act requires prior approval from the **Central Government** for any diversion of forest land.
 
• It focuses on **compensatory afforestation** and the maintenance of **forest density** rather than industrial pollution audits.
 
 
 
• **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**:
 
 
• This Act was enacted to implement the decisions taken at the **United Nations Conference on the Human Environment** held in **Stockholm** in **1972** regarding the preservation of **air quality**.
 
• It empowers **Pollution Control Boards** to set **emission standards** and declare **air pollution control areas**, but specific comprehensive audit rules are typically notified under the broader **1986 Act**.
 
 
 
• **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**:
 
 
• This was the first major environmental law in **India**, establishing the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** and **State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)**.
 
• It focuses on maintaining the **wholesomeness of water** and regulating the discharge of **industrial effluents**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Provision**: The **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** was enacted under **Article 253** of the **Constitution of India**, which empowers the **Parliament** to make laws for implementing international treaties (specifically the **Stockholm Conference of 1972**).
 
• **Environmental Statement (Audit)**: The concept of an **Environmental Audit** was first introduced in **1992** through an amendment to the **Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986**, making it mandatory for every person carrying on an industry, operation, or process requiring consent to submit an audit report for the **financial year** ending **31st March**.
 
• **Scope of Rules**: Rules issued under the **1986 Act** cover a wide range of issues including **Hazardous Waste Management**, **EIA (Environmental Impact Assessment)**, **Plastic Waste Management**, and **Coastal Regulation Zones (CRZ)**.
 
• **Penalties**: Non-compliance with rules issued under the **Environment (Protection) Act** can lead to **imprisonment** for a term which may extend to **five years** or a **fine** up to **one lakh rupees**, or both.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall? A 24 m long ladder is leaning against a wall. If the ladder makes an angle of 30o with the wall, what is the distance (in m) of the foot of the ladder from the wall?

Ladder = 24 m (hypotenuse)

Angle with wall = 30° ⇒ angle with ground = 60°

= 24 × (1/2) = 12

questions.question: Koli is the dance form of the Koli fishermen community of:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Koli** is a popular folk dance of the **Koli fishermen community**, who are the original inhabitants of the coastal areas of **Maharashtra** and the **Konkan** region. ***Hence, Maharashtra is the correct location.***
 
• The dance movements are unique and rhythmic, specifically designed to mimic the daily activities of the fishing community, such as the **rowing of boats**, the **tossing of nets** to catch fish, and the **swaying motion of the sea waves**.
 
• This dance is traditionally performed during the festival of **Narali Purnima** (Coconut Festival). This festival is celebrated in the month of **August** (the month of **Shravan** in the Hindu calendar) and marks the end of the monsoon and the beginning of a new fishing season.
 
• The performance involves both men and women standing in two separate rows or pairs, moving in unison to the beats of traditional instruments like the **Dholak** and **Cymbals**.
 
• The attire is a significant feature; **Koli women** wear a specific **nine-yard saree** (known as **Lugade**) tucked up to the knees, while **men** wear a **Surka** (a triangular loincloth), a waistcoat, and a distinct cap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar:** This state is home to vibrant folk dances like **Jat-Jatin**, which is primarily performed in the **Mithila** region to depict the life of a married couple. Other notable forms include **Bideshiya**, **Paika**, and **Jhijhiya**, which are distinct from the coastal Koli traditions. ***Hence, Bihar is not the correct answer.***
 
• **Rajasthan:** Known for the world-famous **Ghoomar** dance, originally performed by the **Bhil tribe**. Another significant dance is **Kalbelia**, which was inscribed on **UNESCO’s** Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in **2010**. ***Hence, Rajasthan is not the correct answer.***
 
• **Odisha:** This state boasts the classical dance form **Odissi** and various folk dances like **Chhau** (a martial arts-based dance from **Mayurbhanj**), **Sambalpuri**, and **Ghumura**. These dances are rooted in the agrarian and tribal culture of Eastern India. ***Hence, Odisha is not the correct answer.***
 
• **Other Maharashtra Dances:** Apart from Koli, **Lavani** is a highly famous folk dance characterized by its powerful rhythm and **Dholki** beats. Other forms include **Dhangari Gaja**, performed by shepherds, and **Tamasha**, a traditional form of Marathi theater.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Koli community** is recognized as one of the oldest ethnic groups of the **Seven Islands of Mumbai**, and their culture remains a vital part of the city's heritage.
 
• During **Narali Purnima**, the community offers a **golden coconut** or a decorated coconut to **Varuna** (the God of the Ocean) to seek protection and a prosperous catch for the upcoming **year**.
 
• The music for the **Koli dance** is often fast-paced and upbeat, reflecting the energy and resilience of the community against the unpredictable nature of the sea.
 
• Geographically, while the dance is most prominent in **Maharashtra**, variations of **Koli culture** and similar folk motifs can be found along the coastal stretches of **Gujarat** and **Goa** due to shared maritime borders.

questions.question: When was the National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP) launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24th April 2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP)** was officially launched on **24th April 2019**, coinciding with **National Panchayati Raj Day**. This date is significant as it marks the push towards rural economic empowerment. **Hence, the statement regarding the launch date of 24th April 2019 is correct.**
 
• The **NRETP** is an additional funding project under the **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**. It is designed to scale up the efforts of the mission by focusing on higher-order economic activities.
 
• The project is implemented by the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)**, **Government of India**. It focuses on supporting **women-owned enterprises** and promoting financial inclusion through digital platforms.
 
• Funding for the project is facilitated through a loan agreement with the **World Bank** (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development). The total financial outlay for this specific project was **$250 million**.
 
• The initiative initially targeted **13 states** across **India** that were identified as high-poverty regions to ensure that the benefits reach the most vulnerable populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Geographic Reach:** The project covers **13 states**, namely **Assam**, **Bihar**, **Chhattisgarh**, **Gujarat**, **Jharkhand**, **Karnataka**, **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, **Odisha**, **Rajasthan**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Uttar Pradesh**, and **West Bengal**. These locations were chosen based on their potential for rural transformation.
 
• **Promotion of Enterprises:** **NRETP** aims to develop **rural value chains** and cluster-based enterprises. It provides technical assistance and **incubation services** to **Self-Help Group (SHG)** members to start and scale up small businesses in sectors like **agriculture**, **livestock**, and **non-farm sectors**.
 
• **Digital Finance:** A key feature of the project is the deployment of **BC Sakhis** (Business Correspondent Sakhis). This initiative ensures that **banking services** reach the doorstep of rural households, facilitating **digital payments** and **financial literacy**.
 
• **Organic Farming:** The project encourages **sustainable agriculture** by supporting **organic farming** practices. It helps farmers in getting **certification** and establishing market linkages for **organic produce**, thereby increasing the **income** of rural households.
 
• **Gender Focus:** The project is heavily gender-centric, aiming to increase the **participation of women** in the local economy. It empowers **women** through **Producer Organizations** and ensures they have a voice in **decision-making** processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with DAY-NRLM:** While **DAY-NRLM** focuses on **poverty alleviation** and **social mobilization**, **NRETP** moves a step further by focusing on **economic transformation** through **market-led interventions** and **enterprise development**.
 
• **Convergence:** The project emphasizes **convergence** with other government schemes like **MGNREGA** and **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana** to maximize the **impact** on rural livelihoods and **employment** generation.
 
• **Year 2019 Significance:** The **year 2019** was a landmark for rural development in **India**, as the **Ministry of Rural Development** intensified efforts to integrate **technology** and **finance** into the **SHG** ecosystem.
 
• **Monitoring and Evaluation:** The project utilizes a robust **Management Information System (MIS)** to track the **progress** of **rural enterprises** and the **socio-economic** growth of the beneficiaries in real-time.

questions.question: Which among the following commissions in India has submitted a report titled 'Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance'?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Administrative Reforms Commission (ARC)** was constituted on **31 August 2005**. It was tasked with suggesting measures to achieve a proactive, responsive, accountable, sustainable, and efficient administration for the country at all levels of the government.
 
• The commission was chaired by **Shri M. Veerappa Moily**. However, after he resigned, **Shri V. Ramachandran** took over the chairmanship for the remaining duration.
 
• The commission submitted its **first report** titled **"Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance"** in **June 2006**. This report emphasized that the **Right to Information (RTI)** is a fundamental prerequisite for **good governance** and transparency in administrative processes.
 
• The report argued that the **RTI Act, 2005**, provides a potent weapon to the citizens to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority. It specifically recommended the repeal of certain sections of the **Official Secrets Act, 1923**, to ensure the spirit of openness prevails.
 
• The commission concluded that for the RTI to be an effective tool, there must be a change in the mindset of the bureaucracy from "secrecy" to "disclosure." ***Hence, the option regarding the Second Administrative Reforms Commission is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **First ARC** was established on **5 January 1966**.
 
• It was initially headed by **Shri Morarji Desai**, and later by **Shri K. Hanumanthaiah** after Desai became the Deputy Prime Minister of India.
 
• This commission submitted **20 reports** covering various aspects like **Personnel Administration**, **Center-State Relations**, and **Financial Administration** before it was wound up in **1970**.
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Commission:**
 
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was set up in **June 1983** by the Central Government of India.
 
• It was headed by **Justice Ranjit Singh Sarkaria**, a retired judge of the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• Its primary mandate was to examine the relationship and balance of power between **state and central governments** in the country and suggest changes within the framework of the **Constitution of India**. It submitted its final report in **1988**.
 
 
 
• **Punchhi Commission:**
 
 
• The **Punchhi Commission** was constituted by the Government of India in **April 2007**.
 
• It was chaired by **Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi**, former **Chief Justice of India**.
 
• The commission's objective was to take a fresh look at the relative roles and responsibilities of the various levels of government and their interactions, especially in light of the changes in the **Indian economy** and polity since the Sarkaria Commission. It submitted its report in **March 2010**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which class of vertebrates possesses cold-blooded characteristics and scaly skin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reptilia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reptilia** is a class of **vertebrates** that are primarily **terrestrial** and are characterized by their **creeping** or **crawling** mode of locomotion.
 
• Animals in this class are **Poikilotherms** (cold-blooded), meaning they lack the physiological mechanism to maintain a constant internal body temperature and instead rely on environmental heat sources. ***Hence, the description matches the characteristics of Reptilia.***
 
• The body of a reptile is covered by **dry and cornified skin**, featuring **epidermal scales** or **scutes** that provide protection and prevent **desiccation** (water loss).
 
• Most reptiles possess a **three-chambered heart** (two atria and one partially divided ventricle); however, **crocodiles** are a notable exception with a **four-chambered heart**.
 
• They are **oviparous**, laying **cleidoic eggs** (eggs with a protective shell) on land, and development is **direct** without a larval stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amphibia**:

 
 
• Members of this class can live in both **aquatic** and **terrestrial** habitats.
 
• While they are **cold-blooded** like reptiles, their skin is **smooth and moist** (without scales) and often functions as a respiratory organ. ***Hence, Option B is incorrect.***
 
• They usually undergo **metamorphosis**, starting life with **gills** in water and developing **lungs** as adults.
 
 
 
• **Mammalia**:
 
 
• Mammals are **Homeothermic** (warm-blooded) animals that can maintain a constant body temperature regardless of the environment.
 
• Their skin is characterized by the presence of **hair** or **fur** and contains **sweat glands** and **sebaceous glands**. ***Hence, Option C is incorrect.***
 
• The most unique feature is the presence of **mammary glands** used to nourish the young ones with milk.
 
 
 
• **Aves**:
 
 
• This class includes all **birds**, which are **warm-blooded** vertebrates.
 
• Instead of scales on the body, they possess **feathers**, although scales can be found on their **hind limbs**. ***Hence, Option D is incorrect.***
 
• They have **hollow bones** (pneumatic bones) and their **forelimbs** are modified into **wings** for flight.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tympanum**: In both reptiles and amphibians, the **tympanum** represents the ear as they lack an external ear opening.
 
• **Excretion**: Reptiles are generally **uricotelic**, meaning they excrete nitrogenous waste in the form of **uric acid** pellets or paste, which is a vital adaptation for **conserving water** in arid environments.
 
• **Taxonomy**: The study of reptiles and amphibians is known as **Herpetology**.
 
• **Evolutionary Significance**: Reptiles were the first vertebrates to become fully adapted to life on land due to the evolution of the **amniotic egg**, which removed the requirement for water during reproduction.
 
• **Examples**: Common examples include **Chelone** (Turtle), **Testudo** (Tortoise), **Chameleon** (Tree lizard), **Calotes** (Garden lizard), **Crocodylus** (Crocodile), and poisonous snakes like **Naja** (Cobra) and **Vipera** (Viper).

questions.question: _______ is measured using the unit "quintal".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weight** (often used synonymously with **mass** in commercial contexts) is measured using the unit **quintal**. A **quintal** is a historical unit of mass in many countries which is usually defined as **100 base units** of either pounds or kilograms. ***Hence, statement C is correct.***
 
• In the **metric system**, specifically in countries like **India**, **France**, and **Albania**, one **quintal** is exactly equal to **100 kilograms (kg)**. It is a widely used unit for measuring large quantities of **agricultural produce** such as **wheat**, **rice**, **pulses**, and **sugar**.
 
• **Volume** refers to the amount of **three-dimensional space** an object or substance occupies. It is typically measured in **cubic metres**, **litres**, or **millilitres**, but not in quintals. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Length** is a measure of **distance** or the extent of something from end to end. The standard units for length include **metres (m)**, **kilometres (km)**, **centimetres (cm)**, and **miles**. Quintal is not a unit of linear measurement. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Temperature** is the physical property that expresses **hotness or coldness**. It is measured using scales like **Celsius (°C)**, **Fahrenheit (°F)**, and **Kelvin (K)**. It has no relation to the unit quintal. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Metric Quintal:** In the **International System of Units (SI)**, the **kilogram** is the base unit of mass. The **metric quintal** is defined as **100 kg**, while a **metric tonne** is defined as **1,000 kg** (or **10 quintals**).
 
• **Imperial and US Systems:** Historically, the **hundredweight** (cwt) was often referred to as a quintal. In the **United States**, a "short hundredweight" or quintal is **100 pounds (lb)**, whereas in the **United Kingdom** (Imperial system), a "long hundredweight" was **112 pounds**.
 
• **Uses in Agriculture:** In **India**, the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** for crops is usually announced by the government (via **CACP**) in terms of **rupees per quintal**. This makes it a vital unit for **farmers**, **traders**, and **economists** in the **agricultural sector**.
 
• **Conversion Data:** For scientific and trade accuracy, **1 Quintal = 0.1 Tonne = 100 Kilograms = 1,00,000 Grams**. In the context of **bulk density**, mass in quintals is often compared against volume in cubic metres to determine the storage requirements for **grain silos**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History:** The term "quintal" originates from the **Arabic** word "**quintar**," which was derived from the **Latin** word "**centenarium**," meaning a **hundred**. It has been a standard unit in **Mediterranean trade** for centuries.
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:** While quintal is a unit of **mass**, in daily **commerce** and **general science** questions, the term **weight** is frequently used to describe the quantity of matter. Technically, weight is the **gravitational force** acting on a mass and is measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• **Global Variations:** In **Spain** and **Latin America**, the "quintal macho" or "quintal métrico" is used. For example, in **Argentina**, a quintal is typically **100 kg**, but older traditional variations might still exist in **local markets**.

questions.question: What was a major administrative feature in the military governance system of early South Indian kingdoms, such as the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas?

options.text: Temple authorities directly recruited soldiers for village defence
District leaders were rotated annually by royal decree
Military governance was entirely centralised under the royal council
Feudatory chiefs were assigned military and administrative duties

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The early medieval period in **South India**, particularly under the **Chalukyas** and **Rashtrakutas**, was characterized by a **decentralized administrative structure** where **Feudatory chiefs** (known as **Samantas** or **Mahasamantas**) played a pivotal role. These chiefs were responsible for providing **military support** to the sovereign during wars and managing the **local administration** of their assigned territories. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• In this system, the **King** did not maintain a massive permanent standing army for all regions but relied on the **levies** provided by these **feudatories**. This was a **major administrative feature** of the **7th Century** to **10th Century** AD.
 
• Temple authorities in kingdoms like the **Cholas** or **Chalukyas** were centers of **economic and social activity** and often held land, but they did not serve as the primary agency for **direct military recruitment** for village defense. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• Administrative positions, especially those of **District leaders** (**Vishayapatis**) and **Feudatory chiefs**, were often **hereditary** in nature. There was no systemic **annual rotation** of these leaders by royal decree, as stability in the border regions was preferred. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• While the **Royal Council** and the **King** held ultimate authority, the governance was **not entirely centralized**. The vastness of the **Deccan** and **South India** required a system where power was shared with **provincial governors** and **subordinate allies**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The **Chalukyas of Badami** were established by **Pulakeshin I** in **543 AD**. Their capital was located at **Vatapi** (modern **Badami**, **Karnataka**).
 
• They were famous for their **maritime power** and their military conflict with **Harshavardhana** of **Kannauj**, where **Pulakeshin II** defeated Harsha on the banks of the **Narmada River**.
 
• Their administration was divided into **Vishayas** (districts) and **Rashtras** (provinces), overseen by officers who often held **military titles**.
 
 
 
• **The Rashtrakuta Empire:**
 
 
• Founded by **Dantidurga** in **753 AD** after overthrowing the **Chalukyas**. The empire reached its zenith under rulers like **Amoghavarsha I** and **Krishna III**.
 
• The **Rashtrakutas** controlled large parts of the **Deccan** and were major participants in the **Tripartite Struggle** for **Kannauj** during the **8th and 9th centuries**.
 
• Their military was renowned for its **large elephant corps** and high-quality **cavalry**, which were maintained through the resources provided by **subordinate chiefs**.
 
 
 
• **Territorial Divisions:**
 
 
• The **Rashtra** was the largest unit, governed by a **Rashtrapati**.
 
• The **Vishaya** was a district governed by a **Vishayapati**.
 
• The **Bhukti** consisted of a group of villages, usually managed by a **Bhogapati**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Samanta System:** This was a **feudal-federal** structure. **Feudatory chiefs** were allowed to retain their **internal autonomy** as long as they paid **tribute** and provided **troops** when called upon by the **Sovereign**.
 
• **Revenue and Land:** Officials and **military commanders** were often paid through **land grants** rather than cash. This practice contributed to the growth of **landed intermediaries** in **medieval India**.
 
• **Village Governance:** At the grassroots level, the **Gram Mahattaras** (village elders) and **Gramapatis** (village headmen) played a crucial role in **revenue collection** and maintaining local **law and order**.
 
• **Inscriptions:** Much of this information is derived from **Copper-plate grants** and **stone inscriptions** found in **Aihole**, **Pattadakal**, and **Ellora**, which detail the **military achievements** and **administrative orders** of the kings.

questions.question: The telegraph cable was laid across the Atlantic Ocean in 1958 for rapid communication between North America and __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Europe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The transatlantic **telegraph cable** was an undersea cable running under the **Atlantic Ocean** used for telegraphy communications. ***Hence, the statement regarding the laying of the cable is correct.***
 
• The first successful exchange of messages through the telegraph cable occurred on **August 5, 1858**, connecting the continents of **North America** and **Europe**. (Note: While the question mentions **1958**, the historical first telegraph cable was laid in the mid-**19th century**, specifically **1858**). ***Hence, the statement regarding the connection between North America and Europe is correct.***
 
• This technological marvel was designed for **rapid communication**, reducing the time required to send messages between the **Old World** and the **New World** from **ten days** (by ship) to just a few **minutes** or **hours**. ***Hence, the statement regarding rapid communication is correct.***
 
• The landing points for the cable were **Valentia Island** in western **Ireland** and **Heart's Content** in **Newfoundland**, **Canada**.
 
• The project was spearheaded by the **Atlantic Telegraph Company**, which was founded by American businessman **Cyrus West Field** in **1856**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context and Failure:** The **1858** cable operated for only **three weeks** before failing due to insulation breakdown caused by excessive voltage. However, it proved that a transatlantic connection was technically feasible.
 
• **The 1866 Success:** A much more durable and reliable cable was successfully laid in **1866** by the ship **Great Eastern**, which was the largest ship in the world at that time.
 
• **Technological Evolution (TAT-1):** In **1956**, exactly a century after the company's founding, the first transatlantic telephone cable, known as **TAT-1**, was inaugurated, which allowed for voice communication rather than just telegraph signals.
 
• **Materials Used:** Early telegraph cables consisted of **seven copper wires**, covered with three coats of **gutta-percha** (a natural latex insulator) and wound with tarred hemp and an outer spiral of **iron wire**.
 
• **Significant First Message:** The first official message sent across the Atlantic was a **98-word** telegram of congratulation from **Queen Victoria** of the **United Kingdom** to **President James Buchanan** of the **United States**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic and Political Impact:** The cable revolutionized **international trade**, **banking**, and **diplomacy** by allowing markets in **London** and **New York** to communicate in near real-time.
 
• **Submarine Cables Today:** In the **21st century**, over **95%** of international data, including the **Internet**, is transmitted via **submarine fiber optic cables** rather than satellites.
 
• **Global Reach:** While the Atlantic was the first ocean crossed, the **Pacific Ocean** was eventually bridged by the **Commercial Pacific Cable Company** in **1902-1903**, connecting the **United States** to **Hawaii**, **Guam**, and the **Philippines**.
 
• **Administrative Oversight:** Today, the laying and maintenance of such cables involve international law and **telecommunications** agreements to ensure global connectivity across **sovereign waters**.

questions.question: ‘Odia’ was given classical language status in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Odia** was officially recognized as the **6th classical language** of India on **February 20, 2014**. The decision was approved by the **Union Cabinet**, chaired by the then **Prime Minister**, based on the recommendations of a committee of linguistic experts.
 
• It is the first language from the **Indo-Aryan** linguistic group to be granted classical status, whereas the previous five languages belonged mostly to the **Dravidian** family or were **Sanskrit**.
 
• To qualify for this status, a language must have a **high antiquity** of its early texts and recorded history over a period of **1,500 to 2,000 years**. **Odia** met this criterion through various inscriptions and literary works like the **Samanvay** and **Charyapada**.
 
• The proposal for the classical status of **Odia** was strongly advocated by the **Odisha** state government, which provided historical evidence of the language's **originality** and **ancient roots** that are not borrowed from another speech community.
 
• Once a language is declared **classical**, the **Ministry of Education** (formerly MHRD) provides benefits such as the establishment of a **Center of Excellence for Studies in Classical Languages** and two major international awards for scholars of eminence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chronology of Classical Languages:**

 
 
• **Tamil** was the first language to be accorded the status in **2004**.
 
• **Sanskrit** was declared a classical language in **2005**.
 
• **Kannada** and **Telugu** were added to the list in **2008**.
 
• **Malayalam** received the status in **2013**.
 
• **Odia** joined the group in **2014**, making the total count **6** at that time.
 
 
 
• **Linguistic Criteria:** The **Government of India** established specific guidelines in **November 2004**. These include the **ancient nature** of the language, a body of **ancient literature/texts** considered a valuable heritage by generations, and a **literary tradition** that is original and not borrowed.
 
• **Benefits of Classical Status:** The status allows for the creation of **Professional Chairs** for Classical Languages in **Central Universities**. It also encourages research and **digitization** of ancient manuscripts associated with the language.
 
• **Geographical Spread:** **Odia** is primarily spoken in the state of **Odisha**, but significant populations of speakers are also found in **West Bengal**, **Chhattisgarh**, and **Andhra Pradesh**. It is one of the **22 languages** listed in the **8th Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Expert Advisory Committee** on Classical Languages is constituted by the **Sahitya Akademi** under the **Ministry of Culture** to examine proposals.
 
• In **2024**, the **Union Cabinet** expanded this list further by approving classical language status for five more languages: **Marathi**, **Pali**, **Prakrit**, **Assamese**, and **Bengali**.
 
• The **antiquity** of **Odia** is traced back to the **Kalinga** inscriptions and the **Dhauli** edicts of **Ashoka** (dating back to the **3rd Century BC**), which contain elements that evolved into the modern **Odia** script and language.
 
• The **Odia** script is developed from the **Kalinga script**, which itself is a descendant of the **Brahmi script**.

questions.question: If an Emergency Proclamation is approved only by the Rajya Sabha while the Lok Sabha is dissolved, for how long does the Proclamation remain in force from the first sitting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 352** of the **Constitution of India**, a proclamation of **National Emergency** must be approved by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** within **one month** from the date of its issue.
 
• If the **Lok Sabha** has been dissolved or the dissolution of the **Lok Sabha** takes place during the period of **one month** without approving the proclamation, the proclamation survives until **30 days** from the first sitting of the **Lok Sabha** after its reconstitution.
 
• This extension is only valid provided that the **Rajya Sabha** has already approved the proclamation in the meantime. This ensures that the executive's power to declare an emergency is subject to legislative oversight even when one house is not in session.
 
• The requirement for approval within **one month** was introduced by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**. Prior to this amendment, the period allowed for approval was **two months**.
 
• Once approved by both Houses of **Parliament**, the emergency continues for **six months** and can be extended to an indefinite period with an approval of the **Parliament** every **six months**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Emergencies:** The **Indian Constitution** envisages three types of emergencies: **National Emergency (Article 352)**, **President's Rule (Article 356)**, and **Financial Emergency (Article 360)**.
 
• **Grounds for National Emergency:** Under **Article 352**, the **President** can declare a **National Emergency** when the security of **India** or a part of it is threatened by **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**. The term **armed rebellion** was inserted by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**, replacing the term **internal disturbance**.
 
• **Approval Majority:** Every resolution approving the proclamation of emergency or its continuance must be passed by either House of **Parliament** by a **Special Majority** (i.e., a majority of the total membership of that house and a majority of not less than **two-thirds** of the members of that house present and voting).
 
• **Revocation of Emergency:** A proclamation of emergency may be revoked by the **President** at any time by a subsequent proclamation. Such a proclamation does not require parliamentary approval. Further, the **Lok Sabha** can pass a resolution disapproving its continuation by a **Simple Majority**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Fundamental Rights:** During a **National Emergency**, the **Fundamental Rights** under **Article 19** are automatically suspended according to **Article 358** if the emergency is declared on grounds of **war** or **external aggression**. However, **Article 359** clarifies that the **President** can suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of other rights, except for **Articles 20 and 21**, which remain enforceable even during an emergency.
 
• **Historical Context:** **National Emergency** has been proclaimed **three times** in **India** so far: in **1962** (Chinese aggression), **1971** (Indo-Pakistan war), and **1975** (internal disturbance).
 
• **Comparison with Article 356:** Unlike **Article 352**, a proclamation for **President's Rule** (Article 356) must be approved by the **Parliament** within **two months**. If the **Lok Sabha** is dissolved, it similarly survives for **30 days** from the first sitting of the reconstituted **Lok Sabha**.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3, B : C = 4 : 3 and C : D = 6 : 7, then A : B : C : D is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Match common terms stepwise (first B, then C).

A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 3 ⇒ make B same using LCM(3,4)=12

A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 9 ⇒ A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 9

C : D = 6 : 7 ⇒ make C = 9 ⇒ multiply by 1.5 ⇒ D = 10.5

**∴ Answer = 16 : 24 : 18 : 21**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A : B = 2 : 3, B : C = 4 : 3, C : D = 6 : 7

**Formula used:**

Equalize common terms and combine ratios

**Calculation:**

⇒ A : B = 2 : 3 ⇒ multiply by 4 ⇒ 8 : 12

⇒ B : C = 4 : 3 ⇒ multiply by 3 ⇒ 12 : 9

⇒ So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 9

⇒ C : D = 6 : 7 ⇒ multiply by 1.5 ⇒ 9 : 10.5

⇒ A : B : C : D = 8 : 12 : 9 : 10.5

⇒ Multiply all by 2 ⇒ 16 : 24 : 18 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 16 : 24 : 18 : 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combining Ratios

If a : b and b : c are given, first equalize b, then combine ⇒ a : b : c

Scaling Ratios

Multiply or divide all terms by same number to remove fractions

LCM Method

Use LCM of common terms to quickly equalize ratios

Chain Ratio Concept

A : B : C : D is formed by linking consecutive ratios step by step

questions.question: If A's salary is 126% more than that of B, then by how much percent is B's salary less than that of A (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use base value method for quick solving.

Let B = 100 ⇒ A = 226 (since 126% more)

Difference = 226 − 100 = 126

Percentage less = (126 ÷ 226) × 100

**∴ Answer = 55.75%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A's salary is 126% more than B

**Formula used:**

Percentage = (Difference ÷ A) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let B = x

⇒ Then A = x + 1.26x = 2.26x

⇒ Difference = A − B = 2.26x − x = 1.26x

⇒ Required % = (1.26x ÷ 2.26x) × 100

⇒ = (1.26 ÷ 2.26) × 100

⇒ = 55.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 55.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

If A is r% more than B ⇒ A = B × (1 + r/100)

Reverse Percentage

If A is r% more than B, then B is [r ÷ (100 + r)] × 100% less than A

Quick Formula

Required % = r ÷ (100 + r) × 100

Application Tip

Always take base = 100 for faster mental calculations
